sections.text: ## The Big Picture

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: Silviculture is the deliberate manipulation of forest composition, structure, and growth to achieve defined objectives. Every silvicultural system makes a fundamental choice: how much canopy to remove, when, and what regeneration source to rely on.

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
```
SILVICULTURAL SYSTEMS — DECISION SPACE

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
REGENERATION METHOD:
    Natural seed (from above)
    Advance regeneration (established before cut)
    Vegetative sprouts

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
STAND STRUCTURE:
    Even-aged   — one cohort
    Uneven-aged — multiple cohorts

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
CUTTING SYSTEM:
    Even-aged stand:    Clearcut, Seed tree, Shelterwood
    Uneven-aged stand:  Single-tree selection, Group selection
    Specialty:          Coppice/Pollard, Conversion, Strip cutting

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
KEY AXIS: Light-demanding (pioneer) species --> even-aged clearcut
            Shade-tolerant species --> uneven-aged selection
```

sections.text: ## Section 1 — Even-Aged Systems

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: Even-aged systems create a stand of trees all the same approximate age by removing the existing overstory completely or nearly so. They are favored for light-demanding species that cannot regenerate under an existing canopy.

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:

  Before:  Mature stand (70–100 yr)
  |||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||  (canopy trees)

sections.text:
After harvest:
  _____________________________________________  (bare site)
  Seeds fall from: adjacent stand edges, residual seed bank, direct seeding

sections.text:
REGENERATION: depends on wind-dispersed species (pine, birch, aspen),
                retained root systems (aspen sprouting from roots),
                direct seeding, or planting

Seed trees: selected for seed production, wind-firmness, and genetics

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
PROS: Natural regeneration from local seed; cheap

  BEST FOR: Pines (large seed crops, wind-dispersed)

sections.text: ### Shelterwood

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: The most biologically sophisticated even-aged system. Removes the overstory in two or three cuts over 5–20 years, allowing gradual light increase that favors advance regeneration.

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
```
  SHELTERWOOD SEQUENCE:
  YEAR 0: Preparatory cut — thin overstory to ~60% of original BA;
          encourage advance regen; improve wind-firmness
  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  (60% retained)

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice
Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
YEAR 10–20: Removal cut — harvest remaining overstory;
              regeneration now 10–20+ yr old and self-sufficient
  _____________________________________ (new even-aged stand)
  ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ (young cohort)

sections.text: ## Section 2 — Uneven-Aged Systems

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: Uneven-aged management maintains three or more distinct age/size classes simultaneously. No site-level clearcut ever occurs. The "forest" is always there.

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: ### Single-Tree Selection

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
```
  SINGLE-TREE SELECTION:
  Before (cross-section of stand):
  Big|  med  |  small  | large|  med |  small|  Big
  ---|-----  | ------- | -----|  --- | ------|  ---

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
After selection cutting:
  Remove trees individually based on:
  - Physiological maturity (target diameter reached)
  - Poor form, disease, suppression
  - "Cull" trees blocking regeneration
  - Maintaining target diameter distribution

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
TARGET DIAMETER DISTRIBUTION (q-factor / Liocourt's Law):
  +
  | ***
  |     ***
  Count|        ***
  |            ***
  |                ***
  +-----+---+---+---+---> DBH class
  Small  Med  Large  Large  V. large

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
Reverse J-curve: many small, fewer large trees
  q = ratio of trees in successive DBH classes (typically 1.2–1.5)

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice
Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: ### Group Selection

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
```
  GROUP SELECTION:
  Creates gaps of 0.1–2.0 ha by removing groups of trees
  Intermediate between clearcut and single-tree selection

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
Gap size determines species favored:
  < 0.1 ha (200 m²)  --> shade-tolerant species only (advance regen)
  0.1–0.5 ha         --> intermediate species (oak, ash)
  0.5–2.0 ha         --> light-demanding species at gap center

sections.text: ## Section 3 — Coppice and Pollard

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: Vegetative regeneration systems that exploit the ability of certain broadleaved species to resprout vigorously from cut stumps or main stems.

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
```
  COPPICE:                              POLLARD:
  Cut to near-ground level (stool)      Cut at 2–4 m height on main stem

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
+---+                                  +---+
  |   |  Sprouts from root collar        |   |  Sprouts from pollard head
  +---+  and cambium                     |   |  (above browse height)
  STOOL                                  |   |
  |   |                                  |   |
  ROOTS (extensive; old)                 |   |
                                         ROOT

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
Regrowth is FASTER than seed-grown     Used where livestock/deer
  trees because of established root      grazing would destroy
  system                                 coppice regrowth

sections.text:
SPECIES: Hazel, sweet chestnut,        SPECIES: Willows (willow pollard),
           oak, lime, alder              beech (traditional English),
           ash (charcoal production)     ash, hornbeam

sections.text: ### Coppice-with-Standards

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: A multi-story variation: retain selected trees (standards) as irregular overstory while coppicing the understory. The standards provide timber at longer rotations (60–120 yr) while coppice yields regular small-diameter material. Traditional English woodland management from medieval period.

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
```
  COPPICE WITH STANDARDS:
  Year  0: Clear coppice; retain 40–80 standards/ha
  Year  7: Harvest coppice; retain standards
  Year 14: Harvest coppice; retain + recruit standards
  Year 70: Standards reach timber size; harvest; recruit new standards

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
Product:  Coppice = fencing, charcoal, basket material, fuel
            Standards = construction timber, shipbuilding timber
```

sections.text: ## Section 4 — Rotation Age and Economic Optimization

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: ### Biological Rotation vs. Economic Rotation

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
```
  BIOLOGICAL ROTATION: Age at which stand Mean Annual Increment (MAI) peaks
  MAI = total volume / age at harvest

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
GROWTH CURVE:
  Volume
    ^            /-------\   <-- Current Annual Increment (CAI) peaks early
    |           /         \
    |          /           \___
    |         /                \___
    |    ___/                       \___
    |___/
    +------+----------+--------+---------> Age
    Pioneer   CAI peak  MAI peak   Senescence
              (20-30yr) (50-80yr)   (100-200yr+)

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
MAI maximum = BIOLOGICALLY optimal rotation
  (maximizes long-run average yield per unit time)

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
CAI = MAI when MAI is at maximum
  (rule: harvest when current growth = average past growth)
```

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: ### Economic Rotation (Faustmann Formula)

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: Economically optimal rotation accounts for land opportunity cost. It is typically **shorter** than biological rotation because money tied up in standing timber has opportunity cost.

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
```
  FAUSTMANN ROTATION:

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: LEV (Land Expectation Value) = NPV of all future rotations on the site

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice
Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
Where:
    R = revenue at harvest (stumpage × volume)
    C = costs (planting, management, taxes)
    i = discount rate
    r = rotation length (years)

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
Optimal rotation: maximize LEV with respect to r
  --> Shorter rotation than MAI maximum when:
      - discount rate is high
      - timber prices are expected to fall
      - land has high alternative use value

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
EXAMPLE: Douglas-fir coastal Pacific NW
  Biological rotation (MAI max): ~60–80 yr
  Economic rotation at 5% discount rate: ~40–50 yr
  Economic rotation at 8% discount rate: ~30–35 yr
```

sections.text: ## Section 5 — Plantation Forestry

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: Plantations are intensively managed monocultures (or simple mixtures) of single species, typically from selected genetic material, grown on short rotations.

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
```
  PLANTATION CHARACTERISTICS:
    Species: typically 1–3 species per stand.
    Origin: seedlings from seed orchards (bred for growth
            rate, form, disease resistance).
    Spacing: regular, designed for harvest machine.
    Thinning: 1–3 commercial thinnings scheduled.
    Rotation: short (eucalyptus: 7 yr; pine: 20 yr;
              hardwood: 25–40 yr).
    Yield: 2–10× natural forest (site-prepared, fertilized,
           weed-controlled).

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
GLOBAL PLANTATION AREA: ~294 M ha (~7% of global forest area)
  Supplies ~40% of world's industrial timber from 7% of forest area

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
KEY PLANTATION SPECIES:
  Softwood: Pinus radiata (NZ, AU, Chile); Pinus taeda/elliottii (SE USA);
            Picea sitchensis (UK); Larix (Japan); Eucalyptus (rotation 7 yr, fiber)
  Hardwood: Tectona grandis (teak plantations); Populus (hybrid poplar, 10–15 yr)
            Eucalyptus (fiber; pulp; 7–12 yr rotation)

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
YIELD COMPARISON:
  Natural forest (temperate): 2–5 m³/ha/yr
  Managed natural forest:    5–10 m³/ha/yr
  Plantation (pine):        10–20 m³/ha/yr
  Plantation (eucalyptus):  20–50 m³/ha/yr in tropics
```

sections.text: ## Section 6 — Certification: FSC and PEFC

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text: Forest certification provides third-party verification that timber comes from responsibly managed forests.

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
```
  FSC (Forest Stewardship Council):
  +-- International non-governmental; founded 1993
  +-- 10 Principles + 70 Criteria covering:
      social equity, indigenous rights, workers rights,
      ecological function, monitoring, legal compliance
  +-- Chain of Custody (CoC) certification tracks wood through supply chain
  +-- ~220 M ha certified globally (2024)
  +-- Accredited certifiers: SmartWood, SGS, Bureau Veritas, etc.
  +-- Considered more stringent (environmental NGO support)

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
PEFC (Programme for Endorsement of Forest Certification):
  +-- Umbrella organization endorsing national standards
  +-- Founded 1999; endorsed national schemes from >50 countries
  +-- ~340 M ha certified (2024) -- largest area globally
  +-- Considered industry-friendly; less stringent than FSC per some analyses
  +-- Strong in Europe (SFI North America is PEFC-endorsed)

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
COMPARISON:
  +------------------+----------+----------+
  | Feature          | FSC      | PEFC     |
  +------------------+----------+----------+
  | Founded          | 1993     | 1999     |
  | Area certified   | 220 M ha | 340 M ha |
  | Governance       | Multi-   | National |
  |                  | stakehold| schemes  |
  | GMO timber       | Banned   | Allowed  |
  | Controversial    | Various  | Less     |
  | chemicals        | banned   | restricted|
  | Acceptance       | NGOs     | Industry |
  +------------------+----------+----------+
```

sections.text: ## Decision Cheat Sheet

metadata.title: Silviculture: Plantation, Selection Cutting, Clear-Cut, Coppice

sections.text:
| If you need to diagnose... | Start With | Key Caveat |
|---|---|---|
| Pioneer regeneration | Clearcut with replanting or seed source for pine/aspen/birch | Clearcut is context-dependent, not inherently unsustainable. |
| Mixed shade tolerance | Shelterwood over multiple entries | Timing must match advance regeneration and seed source. |
| Maintain uneven forest structure | Single-tree selection for sugar maple, beech, hemlock | Selection cutting is not high-grading. |
| Regular fuel/material supply | Coppice on 15-25 year rotation | Works only for species with strong resprouting ability. |
| Sensitive watershed/visual site | Uneven-aged or group selection, no broad clearcut | Operational access and soil protection constrain choices. |
| Maximum timber NPV | Plantation, thinning schedule, Faustmann rotation | Economic rotation is not carbon or biodiversity optimum. |
| Export-market certification | FSC Chain of Custody and origin due diligence | Certification does not automatically prevent timber laundering. |
| Carbon-credit rotation shift | Longer rotation where carbon payments raise NPV | Protocol quality and permanence assumptions drive credibility. |
